text:
kevin: Heads-up — saw multiple 503s in EU this morning when the primary model pool saturated. Auto-fallback routed a bunch of premium traffic to the quantized variant and support already has a ticket about quality regressions.
maria: Oof. Is this the existing 'capacity-based-fallback' policy? I thought we had tier-aware routing to avoid that for paid customers.
nashwin: We do, but current policy is simple: "first compatible variant with capacity" which ignores quality tiers. That was intentional to keep failover deterministic.
nashwin: Suggestion: add a tier-preference list per customer class, e.g. Premium -> [same-quality-variants, GPU-accelerated-variants], Free -> [quantized, lower-cost].
kevin: Agreed. But need to be careful about cost blowouts. Premium customers can be on Reserved pools; we must not silently spin up on-demand capacity.
nashwin: Right — two levers: routing preference (quality-first) and capacity policy (respect reserved vs burst).
maria: We should also emit clear telemetry for every routing decision. Right now it's hard to tell why a request hit a fallback. Need tags: fallback_reason, chosen_variant, pool_id, decision_path.
kevin: +1. If we tag requests like `fallback_reason=saturated` and `variant_hint=quantized-v2`, we can build console dashboards and alerts.

ashwin: Minimal policy proposal (pseudo-DSL):
```
policy "tiered_fallback" {
  for customer_tier in [premium, enterprise] {
    preference = [same_quality, GPU_variant, cross_region];
    capacity_action = deny_burst_to_on_demand;
  }
  for customer_tier in [free, trial] {
    preference = [quantized, low_cost];
    capacity_action = allow_burst;
  }
}
```

olivia: UX ask — console should show the active fallback policy per route, and a timeline of fallback events (count, avg delta in perplexity/quality if available). Product wants a quick way to "force quality fallback" per customer for A/B.
kevin: Yes. Also we need a "pin variant" button on the route page to prevent automatic fallback for critical tenants. But making that available may require guardrails (minutes TTL, approval flow).
maria: Implementation note: runtime needs to support policy pre-evaluation fast — we can't add a slow look-up per request. Precompute per-tenant preference vectors and cache in the runtime.
kevin: For telemetry, make two metrics: `routing.fallback.count{reason, tier, region}` and `routing.fallback.latency_penalty_ms`. Also store a trace sample with the decision chain for 1% requests.

olivia: Cost concern: preferring higher-quality variants for Premium will increase token cost and could exhaust reserved capacity. Can we use soft-thresholding? e.g. allow up to X% of Premium on same-quality fallback, then spill to lower variants.
nashwin: Soft-threshold is good. Add a cooldown and rate limit per pool: `spill_rate_per_minute` and `soft_capacity_threshold_pct`.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/route-pref-cache -> staging (env=staging, sha=4f9a2c).

maria: Next steps:
- Ashwin to write RFC describing new policy DSL and precompute cache.
- Olivia to mock console UX: fallback timeline + pin + per-tenant preference view.
- Kevin to define telemetry events and dashboards for eng + support.
- Small ops guardrail: deny_burst_to_on_demand default for enterprise.

kevin: I'll sketch the RFC today and post a short PR for the telemetry tags. If we can get a cheap console prototype, product can validate with CS.
maria: Thanks — label this `prio:high` and add to next sprint planning.
kevin: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
